record.what_it_does: Ecommerce platform for online stores, with APIs for products, orders, customers and checkout.
record.auth_notes: All current methods are OAuth 2.0 grants. The authorization code grant is for apps that run outside the admin, and the merchant is redirected to Shopify to approve access. Token exchange swaps an ID token for an access token and is for embedded apps. The client credentials grant uses a client secret and works only for stores in the app's own organization. Public apps can also use client credentials with a client assertion signed by a private key. Tokens can be offline (the default, long-lived) or online (limited to a staff member's session). Custom apps created in the Shopify admin get a static access token, but new ones can no longer be created; existing ones are still maintained. The access token goes in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header. A multi-merchant agent toolkit would use the public-app authorization code grant and store one offline token per shop.
record.access_notes: A developer can work alone for free. Development stores are free and have no time limit, and they can be created from a Partner or Dev Dashboard account. Custom distribution installs on a single store and needs no approval. Public distribution, meaning installs across many merchants, requires Shopify approval. It also requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee; the fee amount is not stated on the pages I fetched. The App Review team can reject apps that don't meet its standards.
record.api_breadth_notes: The GraphQL Admin API is the primary API. It covers products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, discounts, metafields and more, and the Storefront API is separate. The REST Admin API has been legacy since October 1, 2024. Since April 1, 2025, all new public apps must be built only with the GraphQL Admin API. I did not count operations, but the GraphQL schema clearly has well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Shopify's official Dev MCP server is the @shopify/dev-mcp package (npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest). It runs locally without authentication and gives access to developer docs and API schemas. It is part of the Shopify AI Toolkit, which can also run supported store-management tasks through the authenticated store context of the Shopify CLI. That path is local and CLI-based; it is not a hosted multi-tenant admin MCP. I found no vendor-hosted remote MCP for admin operations on shopify.dev. Third-party blogs mention an @shopify/admin-mcp package, but it is unverified. The first pass described shopper-facing Storefront, UCP and Checkout MCP endpoints, and I did not re-verify those in this pass.
record.blocker_notes: Development and testing are free on development stores. A multi-merchant OAuth app needs public distribution, which requires Shopify approval and paid App Store registration (a one-time fee). Tokens are per shop. New public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API, and there is no OpenAPI spec.
